teile.anweisung: Lies den Text genau. Beantworte dann die Fragen.

text: Last September Emma came to a new school in Plymouth. On the first day she didn't know anybody. At lunchtime she sat alone and felt lonely. The other kids were not unfriendly, but they talked about their holidays and Emma was too shy to say hello.

In the afternoon her class had PE in the sports hall. They played table tennis. Emma was very good at it, and she won three games. After the lesson a girl called Mia smiled at her and said, “Wow, you are fantastic! We have a table tennis club on Tuesdays. Would you like to join us?”
Emma was surprised and very happy. The next day she sat with Mia and her friends at lunchtime. Now she wasn't alone any more.

The class played table tennis in PE.
Emma lost three games.
The table tennis club is on Tuesdays.

How did Emma feel at lunchtime on the first day? (one word)
Where did the class have PE?
What is the name of the girl who smiled at Emma?
How many games did Emma win?
How did Emma feel after the lesson? (one word)

text: In the summer holidays Ben and his family went to Spain. They stayed in a small hotel at the seaside. The weather was fantastic – it was sunny every day. In the mornings Ben swam in the sea, and in the afternoons he played football with some Spanish boys on the beach. He didn't speak Spanish, but that was no problem.
One day the family visited a big stadium in the city. Ben took lots of photos there. His sister Lily wasn't interested in football, so she read a book in a café.
On the last evening they ate fish in a restaurant. Ben was sad because he didn't want to go home. “Next year we must come back,” he said.

text: Mrs Trent lives in Park Street. She is old and she can't walk well. Her best friend is her dog Max. He is small and brown, with long ears and a short tail.
On Saturday evening there was a festival in the neighbourhood. There were fireworks, and Max was very scared. He ran out of the garden and didn't come back. Poor Mrs Trent was very sad.

Her young neighbours, Ali and Kate, wanted to help. They made posters with a photo of Max and put them up at the bus stop and at the supermarket. On Sunday morning the hairdresser called Mrs Trent. “Max is here in my shop!” she said. Ali and Kate got the dog and took him home. Mrs Trent was so happy! She gave them hot chocolate and biscuits.

Max has got long ears.

text: Every year on 5th November people in Great Britain celebrate Bonfire Night. Last year Tom's street had a big party. In the afternoon the children collected wood for the bonfire. Tom's dad made potatoes in the fire, and Mrs Green from number 12 made hot chocolate for everybody.

There were some biscuits and nuts too, but there wasn't any lemonade – it was too cold for that! At seven o'clock the fireworks started. They were fantastic. Tom's little sister Amy was scared at first, so she watched from the window. Then she came out with her lantern.
The party finished at nine o'clock. “That was the best party of the year,” said Tom. “Our neighbours are great!”

text: Today is sports day at Hill School. All the pupils are outside on the sports ground. Adam's group is playing cricket. Adam is tall and sporty, and he is very good at it. His friend Jay doesn't like cricket, so he is doing judo in the sports hall.
Ellie isn't doing any sport today. She has a headache and a sore throat. Her teacher says, “You should go home and drink lots of tea.”

At lunchtime the pupils are hungry. There are healthy snacks: carrots, yogurt and fruit. There isn't any junk food. “Yum!” says Adam and takes three carrots. In the afternoon there is a climbing wall. Jay thinks it's scary, but he tries it. At the end of the day everybody is tired but happy.

text: Lucy wants to change her lifestyle. She often feels tired, and she thinks she eats too much junk food. Her doctor says, “You should eat more fruit and vegetables, and you shouldn't drink so many sugary drinks.”

So Lucy makes a plan. On Monday she writes a shopping list: carrots, yogurt, bread and butter – but no sweets! On Tuesday she goes swimming with her friend Sam. On Wednesday she doesn't feel like it, but Sam rings her and says, “Come on, we're going to aerobics!” The class is difficult and very loud, but it is fun.
On Friday Lucy isn't tired any more. “I'm glad I did it,” she says. “Next week I want to try gymnastics.”

text: Mia is thirteen. She gets five pounds pocket money a week. Her friend Zoe gets eight pounds, so Mia thinks her parents are the meanest parents in the world. But Zoe has to do more chores than Mia: she has to empty the dishwasher every day and hoover her room twice a week. Mia only has to tidy her room once a week.
Last month Mia wanted to buy a new dress for a party. It was thirty pounds – too expensive! So she made a deal with her dad: she washed his car every Saturday, and he paid her five pounds each time.
After four weeks she had enough money. But then she saw a nicer dress in a second-hand shop. It was cheaper – only ten pounds! Mia bought it and still had money for the cinema.

text: Last Saturday Ravi and his friends planned a day out. “Let's go to the circus,” said Ravi. “No, the theatre is better,” said Anna. “But ice skating is the best!” said Tom. “And it's cheaper than the theatre.” So they went ice skating.

They took the bus at ten o'clock in the morning. It was only three miles. Anna was the best skater. Tom was worse than Anna, and Ravi was the worst – he sat on the ice all the time! But he laughed a lot. Ravi didn't have gloves, so his hands were very cold.
After two hours they were hungry. They bought chips and hot chocolate. In the evening Ravi messaged his friends: “That was the funniest day of the year. Next time I'm going to bring gloves!”

text: Tomorrow class 6b will go on a hike in Dartmoor National Park in the south-west of England. Their teacher, Mr Hill, is checking the weather forecast. “It won't rain,” he says, “but it will be windy and cold. You should pack warm clothes and good boots.”
Leo is excited. “I'm sure we'll see wild ponies!” he says. His friend Nina isn't so sure. “Maybe it will be foggy and we won't see anything,” she says.

Mr Hill gives everybody a whistle. “Dartmoor can be dangerous in the fog,” he says. “You should always stay on the track. And you shouldn't leave any rubbish – take a plastic bag with you.” The bus will leave at eight o'clock. In the afternoon they will climb to the top of a hill and take a class photo there.

text: Last Saturday Kim and her brother Dan went hiking on Dartmoor. In the morning it was sunny, so they didn't check the weather forecast. They walked along a river and crossed an old stone bridge. At one o'clock they had lunch at the top of a hill.
Then the weather changed. It got cloudy and very foggy. “I can't see the track,” said Dan. Kim's leg was sore, and she couldn't walk fast. They were scared.

Then Kim found the whistle in her rucksack. She used it three times. A man in a cottage heard the whistle and came out with his dog. He showed them the way to the bus stop. “Next time we will check the forecast first,” said Kim. “And we'll take a map!” said Dan.
